company.name: Amwaste LLC
company.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling
company.description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, construction and industrial end markets across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana. The business operates an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by owned disposal sites, transfer stations, and recycling infrastructure. Public materials describe a platform with more than 300,000 customers, eight landfill sites, ten transfer stations, and a materials recovery facility. The company has expanded through bolt-on acquisitions and local contract wins to deepen density in its core Southeastern markets. 3i invested growth capital through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in July 2023, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Founded by Chip Russell as Matter Management Enterprises in the Birmingham market.
Acquired the Sylvan Springs Waste Complex from Meredith Environmental.
Acquired the Whitestone Valley C&D Landfill and four transfer stations from Cash Environmental Resources.
3i North American Infrastructure Fund completed its growth-capital investment in Amwaste.
Acquired Waste Away Environmental in Milledgeville, Georgia.

company.name: EC Waste
company.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, and landfill services
company.description: EC Waste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, and disposal services across Puerto Rico. Its customers include residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal accounts served through an island-wide operating footprint. The business uses an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by disposal sites, transfer infrastructure, hauling operations, and related environmental services. 3i has described the company as the largest vertically integrated waste-services provider in Puerto Rico, with more than 80,000 customers and multiple disposal and transfer assets. The platform has grown through acquisitions, including the 2020 purchase of Republic Services of Puerto Rico and the 2025 acquisition of ARB Waste Services. 3i acquired a majority interest through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in 2021, with management reinvesting alongside the fund.

company.name: Regional Rail, LLC
company.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. Public disclosures describe a network of more than 875 route miles, 17 railroad operations, and approximately 65,000 annual carloads as of 2023. The footprint expanded materially after 2019 through acquisitions in Florida, the Midwest, Ohio, Indiana, and western Canada. 3i invested in Regional Rail in July 2019 as its North American rail infrastructure platform and remains the disclosed owner.

company.name: Smarte Carte International Holdings, Inc.
company.description: Smarte Carte provides self-service luggage carts, electronic lockers, strollers, mobility services, and related passenger services in airports and other high-traffic venues. Its customer base is concentrated in travel, leisure, and public-venue operators that outsource essential passenger equipment and related services. The company combines an asset-heavy fleet of owned equipment with contracted concession and service arrangements across airports and other locations. Public materials describe more than 140,000 owned units and operations in more than 3,400 locations worldwide. The business has broadened its service offering through acquisitions and contract wins, including Aviation Mobility in 2018, Heathrow trolley operations in 2024, and Lost and Found Software in 2026. 3i invested alongside management in 2017 and continues to hold Smarte Group as a proprietary-capital infrastructure investment; the ownership split is not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Stillhouse Solar Project
company.description: Stillhouse is a utility-scale solar project in Bell County, Texas. Its customer base is the ERCOT market and contracted corporate offtakers, including Hyundai affiliates under a long-term power purchase arrangement. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted generation model centered on long-lived photovoltaic infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 210 megawatt AC and approximately 281 to 284 megawatt DC solar facility that reached completion in 2025 and commercial operations in 2026. Matrix Renewables acquired the late-stage project from OCI in 2023 and remains the project sponsor. Northleaf Capital Partners became a minority investor through the Stillhouse TEP LLC tax partnership in 2024; Acadia Infrastructure Capital sourced preferred equity and facilitated an environmental-attribute transaction but is not identified as an owner.

Matrix Renewables acquired the Stillhouse project from OCI Solar Power.

Matrix secured financing for Stillhouse; Northleaf Capital became the Class A investor through Stillhouse TEP LLC, while Acadia sourced preferred equity and facilitated environmental-attribute certificates.
Matrix and SOLV Energy announced completion of Stillhouse Solar in Bell County, Texas.

company.name: Catalyze
company.subsector: Distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure
company.description: Catalyze develops, finances, owns, and operates distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging assets in the United States. Its customer base includes commercial and industrial real estate owners, business operators, public-sector counterparties, and community-solar subscribers. The company follows an asset-heavy independent power producer and developer model, with revenues supported by long-term contracts, leases, and other recurring project cash flows. Public materials describe a national platform active across more than 30 states, and recent financings support portfolios including 79 MW of New York community-solar projects and 100 MW of projects in New York, Illinois, California, and Virginia. Catalyze was founded in 2017 and has expanded through project development, operating portfolio growth, and structured financing transactions. EnCap invested in 2019, and Actis acquired a co-control stake alongside EnCap in February 2023 through Actis Energy 5; percentage ownership is not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Catalyze was founded as a distributed renewable-energy developer and independent power producer.
EnCap made its initial investment in Catalyze.
Actis and EnCap announced a co-control investment in Catalyze targeting the build-out of roughly 600 MW of solar and storage capacity.
NY Green Bank committed $100 million of financing for a 79 MW community distributed-generation portfolio.
Catalyze closed a 100 MW distributed-solar tax-equity financing with RBC Community Investments.

company.name: TERRANOVA
company.description: TERRANOVA is a Latin American hyperscale data center platform being developed for cloud, AI, and enterprise computing demand. Its end markets are hyperscale cloud providers and other large digital infrastructure users that require large sites with secured land and power. The operating model is asset-heavy and development led, with value creation tied to site control, power access, construction, and eventual long-term customer occupancy. Actis disclosed at launch that the platform had secured land and power capable of supporting up to 1 GW across projects in Mexico, Brazil, and Chile, with the first campus located in Querétaro. Actis launched TERRANOVA in December 2025 through its digital infrastructure strategy, and the current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Valia Energía
company.subsector: Independent power generation and gas transportation
company.description: Valia Energía is a Mexican independent power producer operating natural gas-fired combined-cycle generation assets and a related gas pipeline. Its customers are power purchasers in Mexico's electricity market and other users of reliable dispatchable generation rather than retail end users. The operating model is asset-heavy and infrastructure based, with cash flows tied to large-scale generating plants and associated fuel transportation assets. Actis and company materials state that the platform has 3.2 GW of installed capacity across seven plants and a 58-kilometer gas pipeline. Actis created the platform in 2022 through the acquisition of MT Falcon and expanded it in 2023 through the acquisition of EVM Energia; the current ownership percentage is not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Alpha Generation, LLC
company.subsector: Thermal generation infrastructure and independent power production
company.description: AlphaGen manages and operates a large portfolio of gas- and oil-fired generation assets in major U.S. power markets. Its customer base is primarily wholesale power, capacity, and ancillary-services markets across PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, and CAISO rather than retail end users. The platform follows an asset-heavy model built around dispatchable generating facilities and associated development, repowering, and grid-upgrade opportunities. Public disclosures describe approximately 13 to 14 gigawatts of capacity across 23 to 24 facilities in six states and nearly $2 billion of annual revenue at formation. The portfolio is concentrated in strategic markets where reliability, peaking capacity, and time-to-power have gained importance as electricity demand has risen. ArcLight created AlphaGen in January 2024, and ADIA agreed a $500 million minority investment in January 2025; a 2026 New York regulatory ruling identifies ArcLight Fund VII as the controlling sponsor and discloses ADIA's indirect 16.8% interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC.

company.name: Landmark Dividend LLC
company.subsector: Ground leases and digital real estate
company.description: Landmark Dividend acquires, develops, and manages real estate and infrastructure tied to data centers, wireless communications, outdoor media, and renewable power. It serves landowners, corporations, municipalities, and institutions through ground-lease acquisitions and digital-infrastructure investment and operations. Official February 2026 materials describe more than 70 data centers under management and more than 160 employees. company.name: Colbeck's Corner Wind Farm
company.description: Colbeck's Corner is a 200 MW onshore wind farm east of Amarillo, Texas, with 112 GE turbines and commercial operations dating to April 2016. E.ON secured tax-equity financing from Allianz Capital Partners and State Street in May 2016 in exchange for partial interests in the project. RWE now lists Colbeck's Corner in its U.S. onshore wind portfolio; RWE reported a 100% legal and consolidation stake as of December 31, 2020, and an April 2023 Texas regulatory filing identifies an RWE-controlled corporate parent chain. The public record reviewed does not disclose the disposition date for Allianz's 2016 tax-equity interest.

milestones.event: E.ON, Allianz Capital Partners, and State Street closed tax-equity financing in exchange for partial interests in Colbeck's Corner.
E.ON announced Colbeck's Corner had been added to its renewable-generation portfolio in the United States.
E.ON dedicated the operating wind farm in Carson and Gray counties, Texas.

company.name: Great Western Wind Farm
company.description: Great Western Wind Farm is a 225 MW onshore wind project in Ellis and Woodward counties, Oklahoma, that began commercial operations in December 2016 and sells output to Google under a long-term power purchase agreement. Allianz Capital Partners and MUFG completed a tax-equity investment in February 2017. EDF later announced an agreement for Alliant Energy to acquire a 50% cash-equity interest, subject to regulatory approval and customary conditions. The official EIA-860 2025 early-release ownership schedule does not report Great Western as jointly or third-party owned, and current EDF and Oklahoma state sources continue to associate the operating project with EDF. The public record reviewed does not disclose when Allianz's tax-equity interest ended.

company.name: Circle Power Renewables
company.description: Circle Power Renewables is a U.S. renewable energy development platform focused on solar, wind and battery-storage projects, principally in Michigan and other regional power markets. Amber Infrastructure and the principals of Circle Power launched the platform in May 2021 after an earlier joint venture, with utilities and wholesale power counterparties as its primary end markets. Amber's current energy-investment materials continue to identify Circle Power Renewables as a U.S. investment. The platform develops projects through dedicated project companies: 7 Mile Pit Solar is a Michigan development project whose current state-land lessee is listed by Michigan DNR as Copper Country Power, LLC, and is therefore not counted as a separate manager-level portfolio company.

company.name: Biddeford Lincoln Garage & RiverWalk
company.description: Biddeford Lincoln Garage & RiverWalk is an operational downtown parking and civic-infrastructure public-private partnership in Biddeford, Maine. The project comprises a 640-space parking garage, downtown parking operations, utility and public-realm improvements, and funding for a portion of the City's RiverWalk. Biddeford RiverWalk Community 1, LLC finances and operates the parking system under a 25-year arrangement supported by parking revenues and municipal availability payments. Amber Infrastructure's current project case study reports 100% equity ownership and an August 2020 financial close.

Construction began on the downtown garage and RiverWalk improvements.
Federal Highway Administration publications highlighted the transaction as a municipal P3 case study.
The Lincoln Garage opened to the public.

company.name: City of San Marcos Public Services Complex
company.description: The City of San Marcos Public Services Complex is a municipal facilities project in San Marcos, Texas. Hunt San Marcos Development, LLC was selected as the third-party developer; the City authorized a ground lease and acquisition agreement with a facility purchase price of up to $44.4 million, and the Amber-Hunt team achieved financial close in September 2020 under a Progressive Development Agreement. The City completed the complex in October 2021 and opened it the following month. Reviewed primary sources establish Amber's development and financing role but do not establish a current direct equity interest, so the record is excluded from the active PortCo list.

company.name: Durham Region Courthouse
company.description: Durham Region Courthouse is an operational judicial public-private partnership in Oshawa, Ontario. Access Justice Durham Limited is responsible for the financing, maintenance and lifecycle renewal of the approximately 440,000-square-foot courthouse, which consolidates Superior Court and Ontario Court of Justice services in 33 courtrooms. Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of the project-company equity at financial close in March 2007. INPP and Amber currently report 100% equity ownership and a 30-year term from construction completion; Infrastructure Ontario records construction completion in November 2009.

milestones.event: The project received an Award of Merit for Project Financing from the Canadian Council for Public-Private Partnerships.
Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of Access Justice Durham Limited at financial close.

company.name: Future Energy Park
company.subsector: Renewable natural gas and low-carbon fuels
company.description: Future Energy Park is a proposed low-carbon fuels development in Calgary, Alberta, led by Green Impact Partners. In February 2023 GIP announced a conditional strategic agreement under which Amber Infrastructure was expected to invest in 50% of the project. GIP's first-quarter 2023 financial statements said FEP LP's Class A units remained 100% held by GIP and that Amber's expected interest was subject to definitive documents, project financing and other conditions. In June 2025 GIP announced a non-binding lead-equity term sheet with a different, unnamed global Japanese investment partner, and in January 2026 reported that the project was still working toward financial close. No official evidence was found that Amber's conditional Future Energy Park investment closed, so Amber is not represented as a current owner.

milestones.event: Future Energy Park was founded.
Green Impact Partners and Amber announced a conditional proposed 50% investment; FEP LP remained 100% held by GIP pending financing and other conditions, and no closing was found.
Public materials indicated the project had received Alberta environmental approval to proceed with development work.

company.name: GreenGas Colorado
company.description: GreenGas Colorado is a renewable natural gas joint venture in Colorado. Green Impact Partners closed the sale of a 50% interest to Amber Infrastructure for C$60 million on February 23, 2023. Current GIP disclosures identify GIP's U.S. subsidiary and US Infrastructure Investments Holdings LLC as the 50% partners in the Colorado JV. Both project sites began commercial gas production and sales in 2024. GIP reported equipment and design issues requiring remediation, but the latest official ownership update located for this review continued to identify the 50% partnership and disclosed no sale or exit by Amber.
